mainTopic: Valuing theft payments, the חומש and אשם where there is כפל, and whether a stolen animal that grows up counts as changed.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a שומר who falsely claimed a deposit was stolen and now owes כפל. רבי יעקב says his חומש is 'covered by' the כפל. The חכמים say there is no חומש where there is כפל, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says there is no אשם either. The גמרא first tries to prove רב's rule from רבי יעקב: the קרן follows the value at the theft, while כפל follows the value at the trial. רבא rejects the proof by explaining the case as four false oaths, which create four חומשים. The גמרא then explains why the חכמים still require an אשם, based on how they read 'ואת אשמו' in the פסוק, and how רבי שמעון בן יוחאי reads it differently. Next, רבי אילעא rules that a stolen lamb that grows into a ram has changed, so the thief owns it. רבי חנינא challenges him from a ברייתא, and רבי זירא raises a point about a change of name, which רבא answers. Finally, רב ששת explains that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who hold that a change does not transfer ownership, as seen from their view on a changed אתנן. The source for בית שמאי's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages: only a payment equal to the principal gets an added fifth
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from the פסוק 'בראשו וחמשתיו' that a חומש is added only when the payment equals the principal. כפל is double, not equal, so it gets no חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: the Torah says 'its principal and its fifth.' Money that is paid as exactly the principal gets a fifth added. Money that is not paid as exactly the principal gets no fifth added.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opinion of the חכמים, who disagree with רבי יעקב. They say that someone paying כפל does not add a חומש at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בראשו וחמשתיו' tie the חומש to a payment of just the principal (ראש). When the thief pays double (כפל), he pays more than the principal, so the פסוק's condition is missing and no חומש is added.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its principal: the original value
And its fifth: the extra fifth added on top
The extra 'fifth' payment added for a false oath about money
Money paid as exactly the principal amount

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: “according to its principal and its fifth”;
money that is paid as the principal – he adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: מָמוֹן שֶׁאֵין מִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּרֹאשׁ – אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: money that is not paid as the principal – he does not add a fifth.
phrases.notes: He means כפל, the double payment, which is more than just the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא (begun before this section) with the חכמים's opinion against רבי יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חומש is added only to a payment that equals the principal, so there is no חומש where there is כפל.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: no fifth and no guilt-offering where there is double payment
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי goes further. Wherever כפל is paid, there is neither a חומש nor a קרבן אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: the fifth and the guilt-offering are not paid in a case where there is double payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's view. He says כפל cancels both the חומש and the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים only removed the חומש. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי also removes the אשם, the קרבן normally brought for a false oath about money. With this, the ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא will now analyze it.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt-offering brought for a false oath about money
Double payment owed by a thief (or by one who falsely claims theft)

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רבי יעקב says the חומש is covered by the כפל. The חכמים say there is no חומש with כפל. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says there is no חומש and no אשם with כפל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
neither a fifth nor a guilt-offering is paid
in a place where there is double payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא, stricter in removing payments than the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where כפל applies, neither חומש nor אשם is owed.

steps.title: Focusing on רבי יעקב: what case makes the fifth equal the double payment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks out רבי יעקב's phrase 'his fifth is covered by his double payment' and asks what case this could be.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: 'His fifth is covered by his double payment,' the words of רבי יעקב. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It points to one phrase in the ברייתא and asks what situation it describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חומש to be 'covered by' the כפל, the two amounts must be exactly equal. The גמרא wants to find a case where that works. That case will show how theft payments are valued.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches: pointing to the key line of a source
Counts for him / is covered by
What are the circumstances? What case is this?

phrases.aramaic: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת: חוּמְשׁוֹ עוֹלֶה לוֹ בִּכְפֵילוֹ,
phrases.english: In any event, it teaches: his fifth is covered by his double payment,
these are the words of Rabbi Ya'akov.
What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing רבי יעקב's statement in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case would the חומש exactly equal the extra part of the כפל?

steps.title: It cannot be when the item kept the same value
steps.stepSummary: If the item was worth 4 at the theft and still 4 at the trial, the כפל would add 4 but the חומש only 1. So they are not equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was worth four at first and four at the end, how could his fifth be covered by his double payment? The double payment is four, and the fifth is one zuz!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple case, where the item's value never changed, and shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a value of 4, the extra part of the כפל is 4. The חומש on a principal of 4 is 1, because 4 + 1 = 5 and 1 is a fifth of the total. Since 4 and 1 are not equal, one payment cannot 'cover' the other, so this cannot be רבי יעקב's case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: suggesting a possibility in order to test it
At first: here, at the time of the theft
In the end: here, at the time of the trial
A zuz, a coin worth one dinar

steps.confusionAlert: The חומש is not 1/5 of the principal. It is 1/5 of the total (principal plus חומש), which equals 1/4 of the principal. That is why the חומש on 4 is 1, not 0.8.

phrases.english: If you say that at first it was worth four
and at the end it was worth four,
is his fifth covered by his double payment?!
The double payment is four, and the fifth is one zuz!
phrases.notes: 'Double payment' here means only the extra part he pays on top of returning the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to 'היכי דמי' and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יעקב's case as one where the item's value stayed the same.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With an unchanged value, the כפל (4) and the חומש (1) are not equal, so one cannot cover the other.

steps.title: It must be when the item dropped in value
steps.stepSummary: The case must be that the item was worth 4 at the theft and 1 at the trial. Then the כפל is 1 and the חומש is 1, and they match.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that at first it was worth four, and at the end it was worth one zuz, so the double payment is one zuz and his fifth is one zuz?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only case that fits רבי יעקב's words: the item lost value between the theft and the trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חומש is 1, because it is based on the theft-time value of 4. The כפל is also 1, because it is based on the trial-time value of 1. Only in this case are the two payments equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? Introducing the only remaining option

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that at first it was worth four,
and at the end it was worth one zuz,
so that the double payment is one zuz and his fifth is one zuz?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option is rejected, gives the case that does work.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The item was worth 4 at the theft and 1 at the trial, so the כפל and the חומש are each 1.

steps.title: Proof: principal follows theft time, double payment follows trial time
steps.stepSummary: So the קרן is valued at the time of the theft, while כפל and ארבעה וחמשה are valued at the time of the trial. This proves רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that the principal is paid like the value when he stole. The double payment and the fourfold and fivefold payments are paid like the value at the time of standing in court!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the case it just found. It proves that different parts of a thief's payment are valued at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חומש came out as 1 only because the קרן was valued at the theft-time price of 4. The כפל came out as 1 only because it was valued at the trial-time price of 1. This supports רב's rule that the קרן follows the theft and the fines (כפל, ארבעה וחמשה) follow the trial.

keyTerms.meaning: We see / evidently: drawing a conclusion
The principal: the value of the stolen item itself
Four or five times payment for a stolen sheep or ox that was slaughtered or sold
The time of standing trial in court

steps.whatToRemember: From רבי יעקב's words we learn: the קרן (and the חומש built on it) follows the value at the time of the theft. The fines, כפל and ארבעה וחמשה, follow the value at the time of the trial.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule for theft payments: the thief returns what he took as it was worth then, but the extra fines are measured by the value when the case comes to court.

phrases.english: Evidently, the principal is paid like the value when he stole,
while double payment and fourfold and fivefold payment
are like the time of standing in judgment!
phrases.notes: This is the rule רב stated earlier, so this backs him up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal rule out of the case found in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the קרן follows the value at the theft, while כפל and ארבעה וחמשה follow the value at the trial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יעקב's statement in the ברייתא that 'his חומש is covered by his כפל,' which works only if the item dropped from 4 to 1.

steps.title: רבא: the item could have stayed worth four
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof for רב's rule. The case can be one where the item was worth 4 at the theft and still worth 4 at the trial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it could be a case where the item was worth four at first and is also worth four now.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof from Step 6. He says we do not need the item to have dropped in value at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only worked if the drop from 4 to 1 was the only way to make כפל and חומש equal. רבא reopens the simple case of 4 and 4. If that case can work, the proof for רב falls away. He explains how it works in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (the case is the simple one after all)
At first, at the time of the theft
Now, at the time of the trial

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually,
it was worth four at first
and now it is also worth four,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 6 by restoring the case that Step 4 had ruled out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב's rule, that כפל is valued at the time of trial.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the 4-and-4 case cannot work. רבא will show that it can.

steps.title: Four separate false oaths
steps.stepSummary: The problem was that כפל of 4 is bigger than a חומש of 1. רבא solves it: the שומר swore falsely four times and admitted each time, so he owes four חומשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the problem that the double is four and the fifth is only one zuz: here we are dealing with a case where he swore, then swore again, four times in all, and he admitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the difficulty from Step 4. The שומר owes four חומשים because he swore falsely four times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חומש is added on top of the קרן, so on an item worth 4 the חומש is 1. If the שומר swore four separate false oaths about the same item, he owes four חומשים, which comes to 4. That equals the 4 of כפל, so the item could have stayed worth 4.

keyTerms.meaning: The double payment (כפל), here the extra 4
A zuz, one coin
With what case are we dealing here? (the גמרא narrows the case)
He swore an oath
He admitted

steps.confusionAlert: Why is a חומש of 4 only 1? The חומש is a fifth of the total after it is added (4 + 1 = 5). So it equals a quarter of the קרן, and four of them come to 4.

phrases.english: And as for what is difficult:
the double payment is four and its fifth is one zuz,
here, with what are we dealing?
where he swore and then swore again,
four times, and he admitted;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the 4-and-4 case from Step 7 can work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With the item worth 4 the whole time, the חומש is only 1, so it cannot match a כפל of 4.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four false oaths create four חומשים, which total 4 and match the כפל.

steps.title: The Torah allows many fifths on one principal
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his answer from the word 'וחמשתיו.' It is written in the plural, so the Torah allows many חומשים on a single קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah said 'and its fifths.' The Torah included many fifths for one principal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the Torah source for his answer. One item can create more than one חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask why four oaths about the same item should create four חומשים. The plural word 'וחמשתיו' answers this. It teaches that each false oath brings its own חומש, even on the same קרן. This supports Step 8, so רב's rule no longer has a proof from here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And its fifths,' a plural word in the פסוק
Included, added on
The principal, the original value

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reading shows that 'his fifth is covered by his double payment' works even if the value never changed. So it does not prove רב's rule about when כפל is valued.

phrases.english: And the Torah said: "and its fifths"
The Torah included many fifths
for one principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the four-oaths answer in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That one קרן can carry many חומשים.

steps.title: The Sages: only money paid by the principal gets a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים from the ברייתא. Based on 'בראשו וחמשתיו,' a חומש is added only to money paid exactly according to the principal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: And the Sages say, 'according to its principal, and its fifth.' Money that is paid according to the principal gets a fifth added. Money that is not paid according to the principal does not get a fifth added.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the ברייתא, the opinion of the חכמים. This sets up the inference and challenge that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the חומש to 'בראשו,' meaning the exact principal. כפל is more than the principal, so where כפל is paid there is no חומש. This is the חכמים's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (the גמרא quotes the ברייתא again)
According to its principal, the exact original amount
Is paid
Adds a fifth

phrases.english: The Master said: And the Sages say:
"according to its principal, and its fifth"
money that is paid according to the principal adds a fifth,
money that is not paid according to the principal
does not add a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יעקב's phrase behind and turns to the חכמים's view in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חומש is added only to money paid exactly by the principal, not to כפל.

steps.title: Inference: an אשם is still brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the חכמים: they exclude only the חומש, so he still brings a קרבן אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an אשם, he does bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of the חכמים's words. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים removed only the חומש. Since they did not mention the אשם, the גמרא concludes they still require it. This is different from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in Step 2, who removed both.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering
He brings

phrases.english: but a guilt offering, he does bring,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from what the חכמים left out in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the קרבן אשם is still brought even where no חומש is paid.

steps.title: Why is the guilt offering different from the fifth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference. The same פסוק that ties the חומש to 'בראשו' also mentions 'ואת אשמו,' so the אשם should be dropped too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the fifth, that he does not pay it? Because it is written 'according to its principal, and its fifth.' Then he should not bring the guilt offering either, since it is written 'according to its principal, and its fifth' and then 'and his guilt offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the אשם is still brought. It asks why the חומש and the אשם should be treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים dropped the חומש because the פסוק links it to the exact principal. But the very next words of the passage are 'ואת אשמו,' so the אשם seems linked to the principal the same way. If so, the אשם should also fall away wherever כפל is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking why two things are treated differently)
Since it is written
'And his guilt offering' (ויקרא 5:25)

phrases.english: What is different about the fifth, that he does not pay it?
Because it is written: "according to its principal, and its fifth";
then the guilt offering, too, he should not pay,
since it is written: "according to its principal, and its fifth"
"and his guilt offering"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:25. The אשם comes right after the חומש in the same passage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference in Step 11 using the same פסוק quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that, according to the חכמים, the אשם is still brought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק ties both the חומש and the אשם to 'בראשו.' If paying more than the principal cancels the חומש, it should cancel the אשם as well.

steps.title: The word 'את' separates the אשם from the חומש
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer the challenge: the word 'את' in 'ואת אשמו' splits the פסוק, so only the חומש depends on 'בראשו', not the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים would tell you: the word 'את' cuts the verse into two parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 on behalf of the חכמים. The word 'את' splits the פסוק, so the אשם is not tied to 'בראשו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that 'בראשו' should limit both the חומש and the אשם, because they are in the same פסוק. The חכמים answer that the word 'את' before 'אשמו' marks a break. So the limit of 'בראשו' covers only the חומש, and the שומר still brings his אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A small Hebrew word that marks the object of a sentence. Here it is read as a divider.
It cut it, it split it apart
The פסוק (the verse)

phrases.english: The Rabbis would say to you:
The word 'et' divides the verse.
phrases.notes: That's the word in 'ואת אשמו יביא' (ויקרא 5:25). It separates the אשם from the words about the חומש before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reading: the word 'את' creates a break in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בראשו' limits both the חומש and the אשם, since they are in one פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'את' splits the פסוק, so only the חומש depends on 'בראשו'

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: the ו joins the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers that the word is really 'ואת'. The letter ו (and) joins the אשם to the חומש, so both are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן יוחאי? He says the word is 'ואת', and the 'and' joins the verse together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון בן יוחאי would answer the חכמים' point about 'את'. He points to the letter ו at the start of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים looked only at 'את'. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי notes that the full word is 'ואת', and the ו means 'and', which connects the two parts. So for him the אשם is tied to 'בראשו' just like the חומש, and this שומר brings no אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And' plus את; the full word in the פסוק
It mixed it together, it joined it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai?
'Ve'et': the 'and' joins the verse together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the חכמים' reading in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the פסוק is split
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים ignored the ו, which joins the two parts

steps.title: The חכמים: then why write either one?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים push back: if the Torah wanted to join the two parts, it should have written neither the ו nor 'את'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים would say to you: then the Torah should not have written the ו or the 'את' at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's reading. If joining was the goal, the simplest way was to write no extra words at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו and without 'את', the פסוק would naturally read as one connected statement. So adding a ו just to join, together with an 'את', seems pointless. The 'את' must be there to separate, and the ו cannot cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ who gave the Torah
Let it not write; it should not have written

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: לָא לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לָא וָיו וְלֹא ״אֶת״.
phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write neither the vav nor 'et'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's answer from step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's claim that 'ואת' joins the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining would happen anyway with no extra words, so the extra words must be there to divide

steps.title: 'את' was needed anyway, so the ו joins
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers that 'את' had to be written to separate הקדש money (the אשם) from ordinary money (the payment to the owner). Since 'את' was needed for that, the ו comes to join.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי would tell you: the Torah could not leave out 'את', because it was needed to separate ה׳'s property from ordinary people's property. So the ו comes and joins the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers the חכמים' challenge. He explains why the Torah had to write 'את', which means the ו still has a joining job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'את' does a different job. It shows that the אשם (מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ) is a different kind of thing from the money paid back to the owner (מָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט). Since 'את' is already used up on that point, the ו is extra, and its message is to join the אשם to the rule of 'בראשו'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible; it could not be otherwise
Property of the Most High, meaning holy property such as a קרבן
Ordinary property belonging to a person
Therefore

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים: 'את' splits the פסוק, so the שומר still brings an אשם. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: 'את' only separates holy from ordinary property, and the ו joins, so he brings no אשם.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai would say to you:
It was not possible not to write 'et',

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפְסוֹקֵי בֵּין מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ לְמָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט;
phrases.english: to separate between property of the Most High and ordinary property;
therefore the vav comes and joins the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate need for the word, so the ו keeps its own meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'את' is written, it must be dividing the אשם from 'בראשו'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'את' separates holy property from ordinary property, and the ו joins the אשם to 'בראשו'

steps.title: A stolen lamb that grows into a ram belongs to the thief
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא rules that if a stolen lamb became a ram, or a calf became a bull, the animal has changed while with the thief, and he now owns it. If he then slaughters or sells it, he is dealing with his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: if someone stole a lamb and it became a ram, or a calf and it became an ox, it changed in his hands and he acquired it. If he slaughtered or sold it, he slaughters his own animal and sells his own animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a statement of רבי אילעא about a stolen animal that grows up while the thief has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing from a young animal into an adult counts as a שינוי, a real change. A thief who changes a stolen item acquires it and pays money instead of returning it. So by the time he slaughters or sells it, it is already his. That is why the extra payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen animal does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb
A ram (a grown male sheep)
A change in the stolen object
And he acquired it; it became his
He slaughtered and sold; the acts that normally bring the four- or five-times payment

steps.confusionAlert: The thief is not let off the hook. He still owes the owner the value of the animal. He only escapes the extra payment for slaughtering or selling, because the animal was already his.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
If he stole a lamb and it became a ram,
or a calf and it became an ox,
a change happened in his hands, and he acquired it.
If he slaughtered or sold it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא טוֹבֵחַ, שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: it is his own he slaughters, his own he sells.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a stolen object that changes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that grows up while stolen counts as changed, so the thief acquires it. Slaughtering or selling it afterward does not bring the four- or five-times payment.

steps.title: רבי חנינא challenges רבי אילעא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a thief whose stolen lamb grew into a ram still pays כפל and ארבעה וחמשה. That seems to show the change did not make the animal his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא raised an objection to Rabbi Ile'a: If someone stole a lamb and it became a ram, or a calf and it became a bull, he pays double and four-or-five times, based on what he stole. If you think he acquired it through the change, why does he pay? He is slaughtering his own animal and selling his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא attacks רבי אילעא's ruling from Step 17 by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment of ארבעה וחמשה applies only when a thief slaughters or sells an animal that still belongs to the owner. The ברייתא says the thief pays it even after the lamb became a ram. So the animal must still belong to the owner, which means growing up is not a שינוי that transfers ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
Double payment a thief pays
Four- or fivefold payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
According to what he stole, meaning the value at the time of the theft
A change in the stolen object that can transfer ownership to the thief

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the ברייתא has two parts. 'He pays ארבעה וחמשה' is the part used against רבי אילעא here. 'According to what he stole' is the part רבי אילעא will use to fight back in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina raised an objection to Rabbi Ile'a:
If one stole a lamb and it became a ram,
or a calf and it became a bull,
he pays the double payment
and the fourfold or fivefold payment,
according to what he stole.
And if it enters your mind
that he acquired it through the change,
why does he pay?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא טוֹבֵחַ, שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מוֹכֵר!
phrases.english: It is his own he slaughters, his own he sells!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אילעא's ruling in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's ruling that a lamb growing into a ram is a שינוי that gives the thief ownership.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires ארבעה וחמשה after the growth. That payment applies only to someone else's animal, so the animal must not have become the thief's.

steps.title: רבי אילעא turns the ברייתא around
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא answers that the same ברייתא works against רבי חנינא. If there is no ownership, why does the thief pay the old value and not the current value?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Rather, what are you saying, that change does not acquire? Then why does he pay according to what he stole? He should pay according to what it is now!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא defends himself by pointing to the other half of the ברייתא, which seems to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal still belonged to the owner, the thief would be slaughtering the owner's grown ram and should pay its present value. Since the ברייתא says he pays only the lamb's value from the time of the theft, the animal must have become his at the moment it changed. So the ברייתא is a problem for both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what? (introduces a counter-challenge)
As it is now, meaning its present value
Does not acquire

phrases.english: He said to him: Rather, what?
That change does not acquire?
Then why does he pay according to what he stole?
Let him pay as it is now!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against Step 18 with a counter-challenge from the same ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-challenge: the opposing view has the same difficulty from the same source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that growing up is not a שינוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'according to what he stole' clause actually supports ownership through שינוי, so the ברייתא does not clearly disprove רבי אילעא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's view that growing up is not a שינוי and the animal still belongs to the owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the animal still belonged to the owner, the thief who slaughtered a grown ram should pay its present value. Yet the ברייתא says he pays 'כעין שגנב', the value at the time of the theft.

steps.title: רבי חנינא explains why the thief pays the old value
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the thief pays the old value only because he can tell the owner, 'I stole a calf or a lamb from you, not a bull or a ram.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The reason he does not pay as it is now is that he can say to him: 'Did I steal a bull from you? Did I steal a ram from you?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers רבי אילעא's counter-question, so he can keep his view that growing up does not give ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying the old value does not prove the thief owns the animal. It comes from a fairness claim: the thief only took a young animal, so he owes only what he took. The owner still owns the animal, which is why ארבעה וחמשה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
Bull, ox
Ram
Did I steal from you?

phrases.english: He said to him: as it is now,
this is the reason he does not pay that way:
because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The thief is talking to the owner here.

phrases.english: "Did I steal a bull from you?"
"Did I steal a ram from you?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי הַשְׁתָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּלָא מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אילעא's counter-challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the clause, so it no longer depends on ownership.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying the old value only makes sense if the thief became the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: He pays the old value because he only stole a young animal, even though the owner still owns it.

steps.title: Each sage rejects the other's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא prays to be saved from רבי חנינא's view, and רבי חנינא answers that, on the contrary, he prays to be saved from רבי אילעא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May the Merciful One save us from this opinion! He said to him: On the contrary, may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The argument ends in a strong mutual rejection. Neither sage accepts the other's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילעא rejects רבי חנינא's explanation from Step 20, and רבי חנינא throws it right back. Neither sage gives in, and the גמרא keeps working on the ברייתא's difficulty for רבי אילעא until רב ששת answers it in Step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: May the Merciful One save us
Opinion, way of thinking
On the contrary

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can be read both ways. רבי אילעא says growing up makes the animal the thief's. רבי חנינא says it does not, and the old value is paid only because the thief stole a young animal. Neither side gives in.

phrases.english: He said to him: May the Merciful One save us
phrases.notes: Here רבי אילעא is the speaker.

phrases.english: from this opinion!
He said to him: On the contrary,
may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַחֲמָנָא נַיצְּלַן מֵהַאי דַּעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אילעא rejects the answer of Step 20, and רבי חנינא rejects him right back.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole position of each sage.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No specific flaw is named. Each sage simply finds the other's reasoning unacceptable.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the change of name should give ownership
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי חנינא's view: even if growing up is not a physical שינוי, the animal's name changed, so the thief should acquire it through שינוי השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected to this: Let him acquire them through the change of name!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises a new problem for the view that the thief does not own the animal. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the animal was called a 'lamb' or 'calf'. Now it is called a 'ram' or 'bull'. Even without a real physical change, a new name might count as a שינוי that gives the thief ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (strongly challenges a statement)
Change of name: the object is now called something new
Let him acquire them

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to this:
Let him acquire them through the change of name!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view that growing up does not give the thief ownership, from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (רבי חנינא's reading of the ברייתא) that the thief does not acquire the grown animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without a physical change, the change of name from lamb to ram should be enough of a שינוי to give the thief ownership.

steps.title: רבא: a newborn is already called bull or ram
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רבי זירא. A newborn bull is already called 'שור' and a newborn ram is already called 'איל', so no name change happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: a one-day-old bull is called a 'bull,' and a one-day-old ram is called a 'ram.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי זירא's question from the last step. He says the animal's name never changed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא argued that when a lamb becomes a ram, its name changes, so the thief should acquire it through שינוי השם. רבא says the young animal already had the grown-up name from the day it was born. So growing up brings no new name, and there is no שינוי השם.

keyTerms.meaning: One day old, a newborn
Is called
A ram
An ox or bull

phrases.english: Rava says:
A day-old bull is called a "bull,"
a day-old ram is called a "ram."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שׁוֹר בֶּן יוֹמוֹ קָרוּי ״שׁוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's שינוי השם challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise: the name never changed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Growing from a lamb into a ram changes the animal's name, so the thief acquires it through שינוי השם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The newborn is already called by the grown-up name, so there is no שינוי השם.

steps.title: Proof that a newborn bull is called a bull
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves from a פסוק that a newborn calf is called 'שור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day-old bull is called a 'bull,' as the פסוק says: 'A bull or a sheep or a goat, when it is born.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a פסוק to prove the first half of his claim, about the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word 'שור' for an animal at the very moment it is born. That shows the Torah calls even a newborn calf a 'שור'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
When it is born

phrases.english: A day-old bull is called a "bull"
as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב אוֹ עֵז כִּי יִוָּלֵד״.
phrases.english: "A bull, or a sheep, or a goat, when it is born."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first half of רבא's claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:27: 'שור או כשב או עז כי יולד'.

steps.title: Proof that a newborn ram is called a ram
steps.stepSummary: From יעקב's words to לבן, 'I did not eat the rams of your flock,' רבא proves that even young lambs are called 'אילים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day-old ram is called a 'ram,' as the פסוק says: 'And the rams of your flock I did not eat.' Does that mean he did not eat rams, but he did eat lambs?! Rather, we must learn from this that a day-old ram is called a ram.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves the second half of his claim, about the ram, from a פסוק about יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אילים' meant only grown rams, יעקב would be hinting that he did eat לבן's young lambs, which would make him a thief. That cannot be what he meant. So 'אילים' must include young lambs too, which shows a newborn is already called 'איל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs, young sheep
Rather, is it not that...? (leads to the only sensible answer)
Learn from this

phrases.english: A day-old ram is called a "ram"
as it is written:
"And the rams of your flock I did not eat"
phrases.notes: בראשית 31:38. יעקב is telling לבן how honestly he worked.

phrases.english: is it rams that he did not eat,
but lambs he did eat?!
Rather, must we not learn from this
that a day-old ram is "called" a ram?

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a young animal already carries its grown-up name. So growing up is not a שינוי השם, and רבי זירא's challenge falls away.
steps.triggerLanguage: אַיִל בֶּן יוֹמוֹ קָרוּי ״אַיִל״ – דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאֵילֵי צֹאנְךָ לֹא אָכָלְתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of רבא's claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 31:38: 'ואילי צאנך לא אכלתי'. Read any other way, יעקב would be admitting to theft.

steps.title: The original difficulty from the ברייתא still stands
steps.stepSummary: Even with the name question settled, the ברייתא about the lamb that grew into a ram is still a problem for the view that a change lets the thief acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main problem from step 18. It says the difficulty still has not been answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא only removed the extra argument about a name change. The ברייתא still says the thief pays כפל and ארבעה וחמשה even after the lamb grew. That suggests the growth did not make the animal his, which is hard for רבי אילעא, who holds that a change does let the thief acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, either way
It is difficult

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבא's side point to the main challenge from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's view that a change lets the thief acquire the item.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If growing up were a change that made the animal his, he would not pay ארבעה וחמשה for slaughtering or selling it afterward.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that this ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who hold that a change does not let a person acquire an item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Whose view is this? It is בית שמאי, who say that a change leaves the item where it was, and he does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the difficulty by saying who wrote the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, a changed item stays with its original owner, so the thief never acquires it. The ברייתא matches that view, so it does not have to fit the view that a change lets the thief acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
A change leaves the item where it was, with the original owner
And he does not acquire it

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Whose view is this?
It is Beit Shammai,
who say:
A changed item stays in its place,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter ת in round brackets here, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: and he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָא מַנִּי – בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a specific opinion, בית שמאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view, so it proves that a change never lets the thief acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows only בית שמאי, so it does not prove the halacha for everyone.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about a changed אתנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of an אתנן that was changed, such as wheat made into flour. One ברייתא forbids it and another permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: if he gave her wheat as her payment and she made it into flour, or olives and she made them into oil, or grapes and she made them into wine, one ברייתא teaches it is forbidden and another teaches it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This sets up the proof that בית שמאי hold a change does not count. The גמרא first shows two ברייתות that disagree about a changed אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אתנן may not be brought as a קרבן. If the change turns it into a new item, it should be permitted. If the change does not count, it stays forbidden. Two ברייתות give opposite rulings, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given to a prostitute, which may not be used for a קרבן
Fine flour
One ברייתא teaches
Forbidden / permitted

phrases.english: As it is taught:
If he gave her wheat as her payment
and she made it into flour,
olives and she made them into oil,
grapes and she made them into wine;
one teaching says it is forbidden,
and one teaching says it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source behind רב ששת's claim about בית שמאי.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a change does not create a new item.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתות about a changed אתנן.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ברייתות follow בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites גוריון of אספורק: בית שמאי forbid the changed אתנן and בית הלל permit it. This settles the clash between the ברייתות and shows that בית שמאי hold a change does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said that גוריון of אספורק teaches: בית שמאי forbid it, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the two ברייתות are simply בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreeing. This completes רב ששת's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית שמאי still forbid the flour, oil and wine, they must hold that the change does not make a new item. That is exactly what רב ששת said, and it lets him assign the lamb-and-ram ברייתא to בית שמאי. בית הלל, who permit it, treat the change as making a new item.

keyTerms.meaning: גוריון of אספורק, a teacher of ברייתות
They forbid
They permit

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said,
Guryon of Asporak teaches:
Beit Shammai forbid,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's answer: the ברייתא where the thief still pays after the lamb grew follows בית שמאי, who hold that a change does not let a person acquire. We know this from their view on a changed אתנן.
steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement here is about an אתנן and a קרבן, not about theft. The גמרא uses it only to show how בית שמאי view a change in general.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, תָּנֵי גּוּרְיוֹן דְּמֵאַסְפּוֹרַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between the two ברייתות from step 28 and completes רב ששת's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each ברייתא to a different side of a known disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות simply contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that forbids follows בית שמאי, and the one that permits follows בית הלל.

steps.title: What is the source for בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind בית שמאי's view that a changed אתנן is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source בית שמאי rely on to forbid an אתנן even after it has been changed. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 showed that בית שמאי forbid a changed אתנן and בית הלל permit it. Now the גמרא wants to see which words in the תורה each side is reading. Knowing the source helps us understand why the two sides argue.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asking for the source or logic of a view)
The payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as a קרבן

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source behind the בית שמאי position cited in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches בית שמאי that a changed אתנן is still forbidden.

steps.title: The word 'even' includes changed items
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn from the extra word 'גם' ('even') that the איסור also covers the אתנן after it has been changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'even.' This comes to include their changed forms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the פסוק says 'גם' ('even'), and בית שמאי treat that word as adding something. The extra thing it adds is the changed form of the אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כִּי תוֹעֲבַת ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם', which means 'for even both of them are an abomination.' The word 'גם' looks unnecessary, so it is read as a ריבוי, an extra word that includes more cases. That is why בית שמאי say a change does not remove the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even' or 'also', a word often read as including extra cases
To include, meaning the extra word adds a case
Their changes, meaning the items after they were changed

phrases.english: As it is written: 'even'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19, which ends 'for even both of them are an abomination to ה׳ your God.'

phrases.english: to include their changed forms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 with a word from the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'גם' in the פסוק includes the changed forms of the אתנן in the איסור.

steps.title: The word 'these' excludes changed items
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל learn from the word 'הם' ('these') that only the original items are forbidden, not their changed forms.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: 'these', meaning these themselves, and not their changed forms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's source. The פסוק says 'הם' ('them' or 'these'), which suggests only the exact items themselves are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם' contain 'הם'. בית הלל read that word as narrowing the איסור to the original items. That is why, in their view, wheat that became flour is no longer a forbidden אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They' or 'these', read here as limiting the איסור to the original items
And not, which marks what is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: 'גם' includes changed items, so they stay forbidden. בית הלל: 'הם' means only the original items, so changed items are permitted.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel:
'these', and not their changed forms.
phrases.notes: 'הם' is hiding inside the word 'שניהם' ('both of them') in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side's source from the same פסוק, right after the source for בית שמאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'הם' limits the איסור to the original items, so changed items are permitted.

steps.title: How בית שמאי deal with the word 'these'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain what בית שמאי do with the word 'הם', since they do not use it to exclude changed items.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי would say: that word...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to explain how בית שמאי understand the word 'הם', and the full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an unspoken question: בית שמאי also have the word 'הם' in the פסוק, so why don't they agree it excludes changed items? The answer begins with 'ההוא' ('that word'). It will show that בית שמאי use 'הם' to teach a different lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That one', meaning that word is needed for something else

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai: that word
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next part of the daf. 'That word' means 'הם'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to בית שמאי to explain how they handle the word that בית הלל rely on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning a word in the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think בית שמאי have no answer for the word 'הם', which seems to exclude changed items.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי use 'הם' to teach something else (explained in the continuation), so it does not exclude changed items.
